hook: How chips are really designed, in the open

beats.say: Vitalik Buterin wrote a primer on open source chip design for people used to a pure software view of computing, with review from Matt Venn.
Like software, hardware is written in high level languages, then compiled into progressively lower levels. His example circuit simply multiplies a state by three on every clock tick.
At the bottom, layouts say exactly which layer gets which rectangle, and process names like 180 or 130 refer to nanometers of transistor gate length.
